ai.description: *Kaestlea palnica* is a small skink reaching 5 cm snout-vent length. It is bronze-brown with a distinct pale dorsolateral stripe and a dark lateral band. It features a transparent lower eyelid window.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Kaestlea palnica* is distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous pale dorsolateral stripe that extends from the snout to the tail, lacking in most similar skinks.
ai.habitat: *Kaestlea palnica* inhabits the high-altitude shola grasslands and montane forests of the Palni Hills in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations above 1,800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Palni Hills ground skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky crevices during the warmer daylight hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Kaestlea palnica* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 2–3 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, spanning from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Kaestlea palnica* is endemic to the high-elevation grasslands and shola forests of the Palni Hills in the Western Ghats, Tamil Nadu, typically occurring above 1,800 meters.
